biography.plain_text: Brett Blundy is an Australian retail entrepreneur and investor who built his fortune through Sanity Entertainment and founded BBRC. Raised on a small Victorian farm, he developed businesses spanning lingerie, jewellery and homewares. He co-founded Lovisa and remains its chairman, while his investment group also backs private companies in several industries.

long_biography.plain_text:
Brett Blundy kept his first record shop afloat by bunching carrots, unloading hay and cleaning bricks between shifts behind the counter. He took customers' orders and delivered records at night. The poorly located shop closed when its lease expired; a second outlet in a busy shopping centre proved more successful.

His investment in Northern Territory cattle production financed infrastructure devised by pastoralist John Dunnicliff. At Beetaloo, Blundy funded additional troughs, tanks and fencing, allowing cattle to reach more grazing land. As watering points spread, the herd increased from 20,000 to 80,000. Blundy and the Armstrong family subsequently sold the station aggregation to Consolidated Pastoral Company.
